<RuleLanguageLinks current="javascript" languages={[{"id":"javascript","label":"JavaScript (and super languages)","href":"/linter/rules/use-consistent-indexed-object-style/javascript/"}]} />

:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.9`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useConsistentIndexedObjectStyle`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`@typescript-eslint/consistent-indexed-object-style`](https://typescript-eslint.io/rules/consistent-indexed-object-style)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useConsistentIndexedObjectStyle": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Require a consistent style for object types with arbitrary keys.

TypeScript offers several ways to write the type of an object whose keys are not known in advance:
an index signature (`{ [key: string]: unknown }`), a mapped type (`{ [key in string]: unknown }`),
or the built-in `Record` type (`Record<string, unknown>`).
All three describe the same type.

Using one style throughout the code makes these types easier to read.
By default, this rule requires the `Record` type.

The rule doesn't report object types that refer to themselves,
such as `interface Tree { [key: string]: Tree }`, because TypeScript doesn't allow a `Record` type to refer to itself.

## Examples

### Invalid

```ts
interface Scores {
    [name: string]: number;
}
```

### Valid

```ts
type Scores = Record<string, number>;

interface Player {
    name: string;
    [key: string]: unknown;
}

interface Tree {
    [key: string]: Tree;
}
```

## Options

### `style`

Default: `"record"`

The style to require:

- `"record"`: object types with arbitrary keys must use the `Record` type.
- `"indexSignature"`: object types with arbitrary keys must use an index signature.

```json title='biome.json'
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useConsistentIndexedObjectStyle": {
					"level": "on",
					"options": {
						"style": "indexSignature"
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

```

#### Invalid

```ts
type Scores = Record<string, number>;
```
